flagship.headline: George Harrison releases Wonderwall Music in the UK
flagship.summary_line_1: George Harrison's soundtrack album Wonderwall Music (Apple SAPCOR 1) came out in the UK on November 1, 1968, per Wikipedia.
flagship.summary_line_2: It was Apple's first album release and the first solo album by a Beatle, and the clip below is Ski-ing.

events.headline: Elvis Presley hits No. 1 with Suspicious Minds
events.summary_line_1: Elvis Presley's Suspicious Minds reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for the chart week of November 1, 1969, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It spent one week on top as his final Hot 100 No. 1, and the clip below is the single.

events.headline: Abbey Road reaches No. 1 on the Billboard 200
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles' Abbey Road first reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 on the chart dated November 1, 1969, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It was the only album at No. 1 on that chart, and the clip below is Come Together.

events.headline: George Harrison releases Wonderwall Music in the UK
events.summary_line_1: George Harrison's soundtrack album Wonderwall Music (Apple SAPCOR 1) came out in the UK on November 1, 1968, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It was Apple's first album release and the first solo album by a Beatle, and the clip below is Ski-ing.

events.headline: The Beatles tape The Music of Lennon & McCartney at Granada
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles spent November 1 and 2, 1965, at Granada's studios in Manchester taping their contributions to the TV special The Music of Lennon & McCartney, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: The special saluted Lennon and McCartney as songwriters, and the clip below is We Can Work It Out, the single that followed in December 1965.

events.headline: The Beatles play two shows at the Astoria in Finsbury Park
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two concerts at the Astoria Cinema in Finsbury Park, London, on November 1, 1964, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was another night on their autumn 1964 British tour, and the clip below is A Hard Day's Night.

events.headline: The Beatles open their autumn tour in Cheltenham
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles opened their autumn 1963 British tour with a show at the Odeon Cinema in Cheltenham on November 1, 1963, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was their only Cheltenham concert, and the clip below is She Loves You.

events.headline: Parlophone releases The Beatles (No. 1) EP
events.summary_line_1: Parlophone released the Beatles' third British EP, The Beatles (No. 1) (GEP 8883), on November 1, 1963, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It collected four Please Please Me tracks and peaked at No. 2 on the UK EP chart, and the clip below is I Saw Her Standing There.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones release I Wanna Be Your Man
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones released their second single, I Wanna Be Your Man, in the UK on November 1, 1963, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: Lennon and McCartney wrote it, and it reached No. 12 on the UK chart as the Stones' first top-20 hit, and the clip below is the single.

events.headline: Rick Allen of Def Leppard is born
events.summary_line_1: Rick Allen, the drummer of Def Leppard, was born in Dronfield, Derbyshire, on November 1, 1963, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: He kept drumming after losing his left arm in a car crash on December 31, 1984, and the clip below is Pour Some Sugar On Me.

events.headline: The Beatles start a two-week Star-Club residency
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles began a residency at the Star-Club in Hamburg on November 1, 1962, and played there through November 14, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: They returned for a third 1962 stint in December, and the clip below is their debut single Love Me Do.

events.headline: Anthony Kiedis of the Red Hot Chili Peppers is born
events.summary_line_1: Anthony Kiedis, the singer of the Red Hot Chili Peppers, was born in Grand Rapids, Michigan, on November 1, 1962, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: The band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2012, and the clip below is Under the Bridge.

events.headline: Koschmider ends the Beatles' Kaiserkeller contract
events.summary_line_1: Hamburg club owner Bruno Koschmider gave the Beatles notice on November 1, 1960, after learning they had agreed to play the rival Top Ten Club, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: The band kept playing the Kaiserkeller for weeks, and the clip below is My Bonnie, which they recorded in Hamburg in 1961.
